chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Harijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding wealth in which a treasure is found, its zakat is paid. He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Even if it is abundant?' He said, 'Even if it is abundant, I returned it to him three times.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat for a found treasure (kanz) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that found treasure (kanz) within wealth is subject to zakat, confirming this obligation even if the amount is abundant. The narration highlights the procedural diligence of the Imam, who returned the treasure to its original owner three times to ensure rightful ownership before the ruling was finalized, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise property rights and the purification of wealth through zakat.
